- Volume: ~10k queries/day initially; median query length ~15 tokens; worst-case sequence length ~1024.

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>

Hi Asha — thanks for the quick responses. A few concrete points ahead of the call so we can be tactical on Wed: 

1) Embeddings compatibility
- Redwood can accept precomputed embeddings (768-d) or compute embeddings via our SDK. If you provide vectors, include normalization (L2) and metadata mapping (doc_id).
- Pros/cons: sending vectors saves compute but reduces ability to apply model-specific quantization/rotation optimizations.

2) SDK & Auth
- SDK: python and node clients support a /rerank endpoint and a /embeddings endpoint. Example (curl):
  curl -X POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/rerank \n    -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" \n    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n    -d '{"model":"rerank-XL-v1","query":"How do I reset my password?","candidates":["doc:123","doc:124"]}'

- Auth scopes: token scope 'rerank:invoke' for production; 'rerank:dev' for test. We can mint short-lived keys for your CI.

3) Routing & fallback
- We recommend a routing policy: primary = rerank-XL-v1 (low latency variant), fallback = rerank-quant-v1 (cheaper) if queue depth > 3s or memory pressure > 80%.
- Example policy name: brightline-rerank-prod-route.

4) Structured output / tool calling
- If you plan to surface structured snippets (e.g., answer span + doc_id + confidence), use the 'structured' schema flag in the request body to receive JSON fields rather than natural-language text. This makes downstream UI rendering deterministic.

5) Reranker evaluation guidance
- Metrics we typically run: precision@1, recall@k, NDCG@5/10, MRR. For click signals we recommend calibrating click-based relevance with human labels to correct bias.
- Top_k tuning: run sweep over k in {5, 10, 20, 50} for offline evaluation. For online A/B, start with k=10 and measure latency and CTR delta.

6) Data and privacy
- For PII in logs, we'll accept tokenized or hashed IDs. If you need Private deployment for logs, we can spin a VPC sandbox.

I attached our internal short playbook — it has sample requests, evaluation scripts, and a rollout checklist. We'll walk through the code on Wed.

See you Wed 10am PT.

— Karthik Iyer
Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference
karthik@redwood.com

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Next steps: Brightline reranker evaluation & integration checklist

Adding a couple of operational notes from infra/ML infra side: 

- Evaluation plan (short):
  1) Offline baseline: run your historical queries vs current ranker to compute precision@1 and NDCG@10.
  2) Human-labeled slice: run metrics on the 800 labeled judgments Asha mentioned — we recommend binning by query intent (how-to, troubleshooting, configuration).
  3) Online pilot: canary 5% of traffic with k sweep [5,10,20]. Monitor 95p latency, CPU/GPU utilization, and failure rate.

- Labeling guidance: use a 3-point relevance scale (2=Highly relevant, 1=Partially, 0=Not relevant). This maps cleanly to NDCG computations.

- Rollout guardrails: rollback if top-1 CTR drops > 2% absolute or 20% relative for two consecutive days, or if 95p latency > 200ms.

- Pilot infra option: we can run the pilot on Redwood Dedicated with a reserved pool (1 GPU equivalent) and autoscale for spikes. This will keep latency predictable.

Happy to share a short notebook that automates the sweep and metric plots prior to the call.

— Rishi
